title: JNPR: shareholding pattern, announcements and results-calendar all 502 (stale bundled instrument masters); the one surviving institutional-holding proxy is itself wrong by ~44%
repro: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/shareholding?symbol=JNPR' -> 502 {"detail":"disclosures: 'JNPR' is not a known NSE/BSE instrument"}; curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/announcements?symbol=JNPR&limit=25' -> 502 (same detail); curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=JNPR' -> 502 {"detail":"nse_direct: 'JNPR' is not a known NSE instrument"}. Meanwhile curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JNPR' returns held_percent_insiders=0.85939 (matches outside promoter_pct 85.94% almost exactly) but held_percent_institutions=0.038340002 (3.83%) vs outside fii_pct 1.77% + dii_pct 5.07% = 6.84% combined -- understated by ~44%, with no FII/DII split exposed anywhere.
evidence: sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:393 (get_shareholding raises ProviderError('disclosures: {bare!r} is not a known NSE/BSE instrument') when neither is_nse_symbol nor is_bse_symbol is true); sidecar/services/nse_provider.py:359 (same pattern for the results lane); sidecar/services/india_provider.py:136; sidecar/services/resolver_masters/bse_instruments.json:3 ("_generated": "2026-06-09", 62 days before JNPR's 2026-08-06 listing); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:1908-1943 (three 502 responses); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:230-231 (held_percent_insiders / held_percent_institutions values); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P1_JNPR.json:363-379 (outside shareholding truth: promoter 85.94%, fii 1.77%, dii 5.07%, public 7.22%, as of 2026-08-31)
notes: Root cause: the symbol_resolver's bundled bse_instruments.json (generated 2026-06-09) and, per the pack's own T1 trap, the NSE master (generated 2026-06-05) both predate JNPR's 2026-08-06 mainboard listing, so is_nse_symbol/is_bse_symbol return False for JNPR and every disclosures.* lane raises 'not a known NSE/BSE instrument' before attempting any live lookup -- killing shareholding (quarter, promoter/FII/DII/public split, and by extension the pledge check), the announcements feed, and the results calendar simultaneously, for a live, actively-quoted, INR 15,087 crore mainboard stock. The one promoter-holding proxy that does work (fundamentals.held_percent_insiders, via yfinance, outside the broken disclosures path) happens to be accurate, but the paired institutional field (held_percent_institutions) undercounts the true FII+DII combined by ~44% and there is no FII/DII split anywhere -- so even the working fallback can't answer the mandatory subtle-tier question (which of FII vs DII moved, and by how much). Smallest fix: regenerate the bundled NSE/BSE instrument masters on a cadence tied to new listings (or fall back to a live exchange lookup / NSE 'new listings' feed when a queried symbol is absent from the bundled master), so a stock stays invisible to the disclosures surface for at most days, not indefinitely.

title: JNPR: fundamentals.eps (0.74) doesn't reconcile with the app's own net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding (0.918) or any of 4 independently-sourced outside bases -- and the resulting pe_ratio (358.31) inherits the error
repro: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JNPR' -> eps=0.74, pe_ratio=358.3108 (= 265.15 / 0.74, internally self-consistent) but net_income_ttm=522289984 / shares_outstanding=568998442.0 = 0.9179, not 0.74 -- a ~19% gap between two fields returned in the SAME call. Outside truth (pack) gives four independently-sourced EPS bases (1.07 standalone FY26/post-IPO shares; 0.91 consolidated TTM, the pack's own pick; 0.83 consolidated FY26/pre-IPO shares; 0.71 businesstoday, unstated basis, with full arithmetic shown for the first three) -- 0.74 matches none of them within reasonable tolerance; the closest is 0.71, still off by 4.2%.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:210 (eps=0.74); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:201 (pe_ratio=358.3108); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:223-224,226 (net_income_ttm, shares_outstanding); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P1_JNPR.json:315-327 (four outside EPS bases with arithmetic)
notes: The app's own two numbers in the same payload don't reconcile with each other (eps=0.74 vs net_income_ttm/shares=0.918), and eps matches none of four independently-sourced, arithmetically-shown outside bases. Because pe_ratio = price/eps is computed downstream, the unreconciled EPS also produces an unlabelled P/E (358.31x) that matches none of the pack's five outside P/E constructions either (248x-572x). This is distinct from the pack's own acknowledged 'five defensible P/E bases' ambiguity (T2, expected) -- it's a sixth, internally-inconsistent number nobody can defend, shown with no caveat. Smallest fix: derive eps_ttm from the same net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding the endpoint already returns (or, if using yfinance's raw trailingEps deliberately, label which basis it reflects) so pe_ratio is at least self-consistent with the rest of the payload.

title: JNPR: fundamentals.book_value (70.02/share) and price_to_book (3.79x) don't reconcile with the balance-sheet Common Stock Equity / shares_outstanding (60.17/share) fetched in the same collection, and neither matches the current post-IPO book value
repro: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JNPR' -> book_value=70.02, price_to_book=3.7867754 (= 265.15 / 70.02, self-consistent); curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JNPR/balance' -> 'Common Stock Equity' / 'Stockholders Equity' FY2026 = 34,238,830,000 INR / shares_outstanding 568,998,442 = INR 60.17/share, not 70.02 -- a field already fetched in the same collection. Outside truth (pack): post-IPO book value ~INR 91.4/share (as_of 2026-08-27, company press release, ~INR 5,200cr net worth / shares); a pre-IPO alternate ~INR 60.9/share is close to the app's own balance-sheet arithmetic, corroborating that ~60 is the pre-IPO figure, not 70.02.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:204,207 (price_to_book, book_value); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:995-1024 ('Common Stock Equity' / 'Stockholders Equity' 2026); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P1_JNPR.json:193-206 (outside book_value_per_share, post-IPO INR91.4 + pre-IPO alternate INR60.9)
notes: Two stacked problems: (1) book_value/price_to_book don't reconcile with the balance-sheet equity/shares figure fetched in the same collection (70.02 vs 60.17, ~16% apart, with no period label to explain the gap -- FY-end vs MRQ is a plausible cause but the payload gives no way to tell); (2) even the internally-consistent 60.17 badly understates the CURRENT post-IPO book value (91.4) because the underlying balance sheet predates the August 2026 IPO's INR1,800cr equity injection (the pack's own T11 trap, expected -- not double-counted here as a separate defect). Smallest fix: label book_value/price_to_book with the balance-sheet period they were computed from, and prioritise a refresh after a capital-raising corporate action (IPO/QIP/rights) is detected.

title: JNPR: fundamentals.roe/roa/roce are null (provider did not publish) although the same payload already carries net_income_ttm and stockholders equity to derive a basic estimate
repro: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JNPR' -> roe=null, roa=null, field_meta.roe={"status":"unavailable","provider":"yfinance","reason":"provider did not publish this field"}. The same payload's net_income_ttm (522,289,984) and the /fundamentals/JNPR/balance Stockholders Equity (34,238,830,000) yield a basic ROE ~1.53%, in the same ballpark as the pack's ICRA-derived consolidated ROE of 1.18% (2026-09-16 credit-rating filing).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:215-216 (roe/roa null); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:370-376 (field_meta.roe status/reason); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:223-224 and :995-1024 (net_income_ttm, stockholders equity already in the same payload); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P1_JNPR.json:216-234 (outside roe/roce, all bases, including sign flip between screener's consolidated +0.43% and standalone -0.58%)
notes: roe/roce are passed straight through from yfinance's null rather than derived from the net_income_ttm/equity inputs the sidecar already fetches in the same call. Given how unstable the outside ROE figure is across sources (screener's own consolidated vs standalone pages flip sign for the same company on the same day), a labelled derived-and-caveated estimate would be strictly more useful than a bare null. Medium, not high: an honest null is safer than a silently wrong value, and this is a real gap rather than an active error. Smallest fix: compute a fallback roe = net_income_ttm / stockholders_equity (and roce similarly from EBIT/capital employed, already available from the income/balance calls) when the provider field is null, tagged field_meta.provider='derived'.

title: JNPR: fifty_two_week_high/low values are correct but carry only the API fetch timestamp as as_of, not the actual dates (Aug 27 / Aug 6) the extremes occurred -- on a 44-day-old listing where that distinction matters most
repro: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JNPR' -> fifty_two_week_high=282.0, fifty_two_week_low=232.11, field_meta.fifty_two_week_high.as_of='2026-09-19T09:37:07.524496+00:00' (the collection's API-call timestamp). Outside truth dates the high to 2026-08-27 and the low to 2026-08-06 -- 23 and 44 days earlier respectively.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:212-213 (fifty_two_week_high/low values); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P1_JNPR.json:349-355 (field_meta as_of for those fields); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P1_JNPR.json:344-361 (outside week52 with per-leg dates: high 2026-08-27, low 2026-08-06)
notes: The values themselves match outside truth almost exactly (282.0/232.11 vs 282.0/232.1) and the app correctly avoided the pack's own T5/stockanalysis-outlier trap (204.00). But the app has no field for WHEN the 52-week extremes actually occurred, only a generic collection timestamp that silently substitutes for a materially different date -- and the mandatory subtle-tier check specifically requires every as-of date diffed, not just values. Low severity because the numbers are right and this is a provenance/labelling gap, not a wrong number, but it matters more than usual here: this security has traded only 44 days (pack's T5), so a bare '52-week' label with no date makes a structurally undefined range look confidently precise. Smallest fix: surface the exchange's own as-of date for each 52-week extreme when the upstream provider has it, instead of only the fetch timestamp.
